notes: Jinshu053:s0013 names 宣帝 as the Jin ancestral comparison for Crown Prince Yu. Its complete current67-member component is independently established as Sima Yi; that exact whole component is retained, without reopening or projecting its membership.

Songshi340:s0571–s0585 is Su Song’s memorial paragraph. In s0580 Han Wudi discusses the Han/Xiongnu precedent; s0581 continues 至宣帝，呼韓單于稽首稱藩. This genuine Han Xuandi reference is distinct from the Jin ancestral 宣帝/Sima Yi. Reuse of the posthumous title does not identify these rulers as one person.

Songshi340:s0582 shifts explicitly to Tang and Xianzong; s0583 至宣宗時，乃以三關、七州歸於有司 belongs to that Tang sequence. It is excluded from p176 identity evidence, despite its presence in the current name claim. No Tang career or date is attributed to the Han emperor.
